expectations.text: Produces an actual RCM structure: risk → control objective → control activity → type/frequency → owner → evidence → test approach
expectations.evidence: Has risk, objective, activity, owner, frequency, test approach per control, but no control Type (preventive/detective) field and no distinct evidence column in the structure

expectations.text: Covers the core change controls: pre-migration approval, documented testing evidence, developer/deployer segregation (no self-migration), emergency change path with after-the-fact approval, and configuration changes in the population
expectations.evidence: Ticket approval before deployment; documented UAT sign-off; "Developers do not have the ability to independently move their own code into... production"; emergency "retroactive approval within a defined window"; "configuration-only changes... skip the control process" flagged

expectations.text: Describes population completeness (deployment log vs ticketing reconciliation) as part of testing
expectations.evidence: Says auditors pull "the full population of changes... not a manually curated list" but never describes a deployment-log-vs-ticketing reconciliation as the completeness test

expectations.text: Gives test procedures with conventional sample sizes labelled as convention (e.g., 25 for frequent changes) and TOD walkthrough plus TOE distinction
expectations.evidence: "often 25-40 for operating effectiveness over a full year, fewer for design/implementation-only testing" — typical-practice framing plus design-vs-operating distinction

expectations.text: Anchors why it matters: unauthorized billing-engine changes → misstated revenue (misstatement-anchored risk statements, not generic security risks)
expectations.evidence: "Unauthorized, untested, or improperly approved changes to the billing engine could result in incorrect invoice calculation, revenue misstatement"
